clauses.reason: Whole order (single operative paragraph of the held text): the permission to inspect the stated returns is limited to the Ninetieth Congress. Terminated by its own terms at the end of that Congress, recorded as 1969-01-03 inclusive (terms of Senators and Representatives end at noon on January 3 under the Twentieth Amendment, section 1); the alternative reading ends the permission at noon on that day. No amendment, supersession or revocation of this order is held, so there is no earlier end. The reference to the Secretary of the Treasury rules in Treasury Decisions 6132 and 6133 is a condition on the inspection, not a separate command.

research_rationale:
EO 11332 (March 7, 1967, signed by the President as printed at 32 FR 3877), read in full in the registered Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11332.txt (machine-extracted text layer of the official PDF, graded original_representation_unverified and counted as an official original; I did not inspect the PDF page images). The held-text search also returns the capture file for EO 11331, which holds the same Federal Register pages (PDF page 11 of 64) and so contains this order as page text; it is not a later order. Identity: the number, subject and date in the held text agree with the census register. Content: a single operative paragraph. Under section 55(a) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1939 and section 6103(a) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1954, it orders that any income, excess-profits, estate, or gift tax return for the years 1947 to 1968, inclusive, shall, during the Ninetieth Congress, be open to inspection by the Committee on Government Operations, House of Representatives or any duly authorized subcommittee thereof, in connection with its studies of the operation of Government activities at all levels with a view to determining the economy and efficiency of the Government; the inspection is to follow the Secretary of the Treasury rules in Treasury Decisions 6132 and 6133; and the order takes effect on filing for publication in the Federal Register. First end: by its own terms the permission operates only during the Ninetieth Congress, which ran from January 3, 1967 to January 3, 1969. Section 1 of the Twentieth Amendment ends the terms of Senators and Representatives at noon on January 3; its text is not held in this packet and the end date is taken from it as a matter of constitutional law. The end is recorded as 1969-01-03, the last day of the Congress, inclusive; the alternative reading is that the Congress ends at noon on that day. No held source lists the session dates of the 90th Congress (the held House Historian capture covers only the 80th to 89th Congresses), so no earlier candidate date is asserted. Later events: none found. The machine searches selected below (U.S. Code, eCFR and the Federal Register order catalog) have no hit for this order. A citation search of the 33,118 held order texts under jobs/*/output/texts (clause-drafts excluded) for the forms Executive Order 11332, Order No. 11332 and E.O. 11332 finds only the capture of the order itself. I also read the held text of EO 12553 (51 FR 7237) and its table of revoked orders does not print the number 11332. A general later revocation would in any case fall after the own-terms end. The order is read as terminated at the cutoff 2026-10-14 by its own terms; the standing disclosure that this order rests on a Federal Register OCR text layer and not on an authenticated original applies.

savings.reason: The order contains no savings, transition or retention language. Inspections made during the Ninetieth Congress were completed acts, and nothing in the order governs how information obtained from the returns is kept or used afterwards, so no independent command or accrued right continues after the end of the Congress.
